capabilities: Import Zotero items and extract PDF text with Docling, including OCR
Index document chunks in Redis for local vector retrieval
Answer questions over the library with grounded, clickable citations
Sync metadata and annotations bidirectionally between Zotero and notes
Edit chunk text in notes and incrementally reindex only changed chunks
extras: Desktop-only. Heavy prerequisites: Docker/Podman running a Redis Stack container plus a Python worker, and a local or cloud LLM server. First startup can take 10+ minutes while images build. API keys are stored in plugin settings masked but not encrypted at rest. The README includes a detailed security disclosure (filesystem access, child processes, clipboard, third-party services) and troubleshooting section; the plugin has no telemetry.
motivation: The author built it because Zotero is the source of truth for references and Obsidian is where the user thinks, and nothing connected the two.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to ask questions over a Zotero literature library and get answers grounded in the PDFs with clickable citations back to the source.

relations.evidence: Zotero is your source of truth for references, and Obsidian is where you think. This plugin connects them
For citekey, Zotero -> note sync always applies (including Better BibTeX-generated keys).
Open LM Studio and start the local server.
Install Ollama and ensure the daemon is running

requires.name: LM Studio, Ollama, or OpenAI-compatible server
Cloud LLM / Zotero Web API / PaddleOCR API keys
Zotero companion XPI for annotation images

summary: RAG assistant that imports Zotero items, extracts and OCRs their PDFs into a Redis vector index, and answers questions with chunk-level citations.
